correctness.rationale: The finite local obstruction was independently exhausted over all residue classes modulo 8 and has zero solutions. Therefore an integral or \(2\)-adic point cannot exist. For the fibre, writing a rational coordinate as a reduced fraction yields two coprime quadratic forms whose product must be a square; the parity and square classes modulo 8 rule out both sign branches, while the projective boundary would require a nonsquare rational ratio. This supports rational-point emptiness of the fibre as stated.
